# Naim Montazeri, Ph.D.

## Microbial Food Safety \| Predictive Modeling \| Risk Assessment

I am an Assistant Professor at the University of Florida with over 15 years of experience in Microbial Food Safety (bacteria and viruses), risk assessment, and predictive modeling. My work integrates experimental microbiology with data-driven analysis, including R-based modeling and simulation, to evaluate pathogen persistence, transfer, and control in foods and agricultural systems. I have particular experience working with high-risk ready-to-eat (RTE) foods and agricultural water systems, applying risk-based strategies that support food safety decision-making and regulatory compliance, with working knowledge of regulatory and standard methods including FDA BAM, ISO, ASTM, AOAC, and EPA-aligned protocols.

My work is inherently cross-functional, combining microbiology, data analysis, and applied food safety with science communication, stakeholder outreach, and mentoring of students and research personnel. I routinely translate complex microbiological data into actionable insights for diverse audiences, including industry, regulators, and academic collaborators.

Prior to my current role, I worked on sanitation validation, product development, processing, and quality evaluation in both laboratory and pilot-scale environments. This includes validating antimicrobial interventions and sanitation systems, optimizing cooking and processing parameters for microbial safety, and assessing product quality attributes such as sensory performance and stability. This experience allows me to connect microbiological risk with practical processing, product performance, and R&D-driven decision making.
:::
